prompt: Assume hypothetical 40% bitrate savings for AV1 at equal quality, with an extra $0.40 encode cost for a 10-minute video. For a hypothetical $0.01/GB egress rate and 2.5Mbps H.264 stream, how many minutes watched recover that extra cost?

options.explanation: Wrong. The measured units require bits-to-bytes conversion and pricing every saved byte. Even forgetting the divide-by-eight conversion would not justify a fifty-minute threshold.
Wrong. Three hundred sixty watched minutes save 2.7 GB under these inputs, worth only $0.027. That does not recover the additional $0.40 encode cost.
Correct. Each watched minute saves 7.5 MB, worth $0.000075 at the hypothetical price. About 5,333 minutes recover $0.40; the worked example defines and calculates this model.

options.text: It never pays off, because CPU is always more expensive than bandwidth
options.explanation: Wrong. The encode cost is paid once while savings recur on compatible views. Under the hypothetical positive-saving model, enough watched minutes can repay the encode; real extra costs and device support must also be counted.

workedExample:
Find the bytes saved per minute watched, price them, then divide the one-off encode cost by that saving.

```formula
S = r × 60 s / 8
S = 2.5 Mbps × 60 s / 8 = 18.75 MB
where
S: size of one minute of the H.264 stream, in megabytes (MB)
r: the stream bitrate, in megabits per second (Mbps); here 2.5
60 s: one minute in seconds
8: bits per byte
Mbps: megabits per second
s: seconds
MB: megabytes, 1,000,000 bytes
In words: one minute of a 2.5 megabit-per-second stream is 18.75 megabytes.
```

```formula
v = p × S × u
v = 0.4 × 0.01875 GB/min × $0.01/GB
v = $0.000075/min
M = E / v
M = $0.40 / ($0.000075/min)
M ≈ 5,333 min
where
v: money saved per minute watched in AV1, in US dollars per minute ($/min)
p: the fraction of bits AV1 saves; 40% = 0.4
S: H.264 payload per watched minute, 18.75 megabytes per minute (MB/min), or 0.01875 GB/min
u: the egress price, in dollars per gigabyte ($/GB)
M: minutes watched to break even
E: the extra one-off encode cost, $0.40
GB: gigabytes, 1,000 MB
$: US dollars
min: minutes
≈: approximately equal to
In words: each minute watched saves 7.5 MB, worth $0.000075, so about 5,333 minutes are needed to repay $0.40.
```

That is about 533 complete 10-minute views. This covers only the stated encode/egress terms and viewers actually receiving AV1; storage, device support and other costs can shift the threshold.
